sub_scenario.family: review and decision quality under interruption density versus protected focused work
sub_scenario.one_line: pharmacovigilance case lead: defer inbox coverage pending safeguards

dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the case narrative and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The safety inbox review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
I acknowledged a routine safety inbox item within minutes.
Was a medical assessment underway?
No, I was routing the item rather than building a chronology.
Someone new shadowed me in the review room this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the signal weeks into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
For a liver-injury report, I silenced noncritical inbox alerts, aligned the laboratory timeline with dosing changes, and recommended follow-up rather than a premature signal escalation.
What supported that judgment?
The chronology remained intact through the alternative explanations.
I joined a brief team huddle after a standard case day.
Did that involve causality review?
No, it was a workload and deadline check.
I archived last cycle's notes on the safety inbox and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Our case handbook permits immediate interruptions during review only for a new death report or a regulatory deadline due that day.
Why not answer all incoming cases?
Most can be triaged without breaking the current medical chronology.
A vendor call about the case narrative ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the review room checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the signal weeks.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the safety inbox records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
On an earlier neuropathy case, I answered team messages between source documents and treated a pre-existing symptom as treatment-emergent, sending the case for unnecessary escalation.
What did the restart obscure?
The baseline note at the start of the timeline.
I sketched next week's plan for the signal weeks before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the case narrative updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
A colleague can screen the inbox and bring only death reports or same-day deadlines to the review room.
Would that leave other reports unattended?
No, they remain logged and are addressed at the next triage point.
I compared two options for the safety inbox tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the review room handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
Before I commit to covering the live safety inbox during a complex causality review, what should I arrange?
